An oncoprint is the standard way to show a **mutation landscape**: genes down one axis, tumours
along the other, each cell stacking the alterations that gene carries in that sample — copy-number
amplification/deletion plus mutation type — with per-gene (or per-sample) frequencies alongside. In
R the usual tool is `ComplexHeatmap::oncoPrint`. Here we build an interactive one with
[canvasXpress](https://canvasxpress.org), from a single portable spec.

## The data shape

An oncoprint is a `Heatmap` with **overlay matrices**: a base matrix (`y`, here expression) plus
same-shaped layers for copy-number (`data2`) and mutation (`data3`). Each overlay cell is a string
like `"Amplification"`, `"Missense"`, or `""` for none.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(canvasXpress)

set.seed(5)
genes   <- c("TP53", "KRAS", "PIK3CA", "PTEN", "EGFR", "BRAF",
             "APC", "RB1", "NF1", "MYC", "CDKN2A", "ARID1A")
samples <- sprintf("T%02d", 1:28)
mutrate <- setNames(pmax(0.05, 0.5 * (1 - (seq_along(genes) - 1) / length(genes))), genes)

base <- matrix(round(rnorm(length(genes) * length(samples)), 2),
               nrow = length(genes), dimnames = list(genes, samples))

CNA <- c("Amplification", "Deletion"); MUT <- c("Missense", "Nonsense", "Truncating")
cna <- mut <- matrix("", length(genes), length(samples), dimnames = list(genes, samples))
for (g in genes) for (s in samples) {
  if (runif(1) < mutrate[g])       mut[g, s] <- sample(MUT, 1)
  if (runif(1) < mutrate[g] * 0.5) cna[g, s] <- sample(CNA, 1)
}

smpAnnot <- data.frame(Subtype = sample(c("Basal", "Luminal", "HER2"), length(samples), replace = TRUE),
                      row.names = samples)
varAnnot <- data.frame(Pathway = rep(c("TSG", "Oncogene"), length.out = length(genes)),
                      row.names = genes)
```

## The plot

Pass the overlays in a named `data` list and point `oncoprintCNA` / `oncoprintMUT` at them. `xAxis`
lists the samples.

```{r}
canvasXpress(
  data          = list(y = base, data2 = cna, data3 = mut),
  smpAnnot      = smpAnnot, varAnnot = varAnnot,
  graphType     = "Heatmap",
  oncoprintCNA  = "data2", oncoprintMUT = "data3",
  overlaysThickness = 100,
  xAxis         = as.list(samples),
  title         = "Mutation landscape: 12 genes across 28 tumours",
  width         = 820, height = 440
)
```

canvasXpress sorts the waterfall for you and shows the alteration frequency per row. Hover a cell to
read the exact alteration; swap the overlays for your own MAF / CNA calls.

## Why "reproducible"

The base matrix, the overlays and the `config` **are** the figure — one portable spec. The same spec
renders the identical oncoprint from Python or JavaScript, and can be validated and re-rendered later.
